name: WP Extended – Modular WordPress Toolkit
author: WP Extended

sections.description:
Stop installing another plugin for every small WordPress job.

WP Extended is a modular WordPress toolkit for the everyday jobs that usually send you searching for another plugin.

  • Need to duplicate a page?
  • Configure SMTP email?
  • Upload SVG files?
  • Manage code snippets?
  • Switch between users?
  • Change your WordPress login URL?
  • Reorder content?
  • Put a site into maintenance mode?

WP Extended brings these tools — and many more — into one consistent plugin. Enable what your site needs. Leave the rest off.

One toolkit. Individual modules.

WP Extended is not designed around activating everything. Each capability is managed as its own module, so you choose the tools that fit your site.

Enable a handful of modules on one WordPress site. Use a completely different combination on another. The same familiar toolkit sits underneath both.

With WP Extended you can:

  • Reduce reliance on small, single-purpose plugins
  • Enable only the modules your site actually needs
  • Manage everyday WordPress tools from one consistent interface
  • Keep familiar workflows across the sites you build and maintain
  • Start with useful functionality in the free plugin
  • Add Pro functionality later where your workflow requires it

Everyday WordPress jobs. One familiar toolkit.

  • Duplicate Posts & Pages – Duplicate existing posts and pages without rebuilding the content or layout from scratch. Useful for landing pages, service pages, repeatable content structures and editorial workflows.
  • SMTP Email – Configure WordPress email delivery through SMTP instead of adding another dedicated email plugin. Useful for site notifications, contact form delivery and transactional WordPress email.
  • Code Snippets – Manage PHP, HTML, CSS and JavaScript snippets without editing your theme files. Keep small site customisations easier to find and maintain.
  • SVG File Upload – Add SVG support to the WordPress media workflow for trusted logos, icons and scalable assets.
  • User Switching – Switch between WordPress user accounts more quickly when testing permissions, troubleshooting issues or supporting users.
  • Post Type Order – Reorder posts, pages and supported post types without writing custom code.
  • Export Posts & Export Users – Export WordPress content and user data for reporting, migrations, audits and other workflows.
  • Custom Login URL – Change the standard WordPress login path from the default URL.
  • Limit Login Attempts – Restrict repeated login attempts and reduce common brute-force login activity.
  • Maintenance Mode – Show visitors an appropriate maintenance page while work is taking place behind the scenes.
  • Menu Editor – Rename, reorder or hide WordPress admin menu items to create a cleaner admin experience.
  • Rollback Manager – Roll WordPress.org plugins or themes back to an earlier version when an update causes a problem.

Browse every WP Extended module

Built around the way you actually use WordPress.

A large toolkit does not mean every feature should be active. That is why WP Extended is modular.

Turn on SMTP on one site. Use Code Snippets and SVG uploads on another. Add content, admin or login tools where they make sense. Leave everything else disabled.

Turn on what you need. Leave the rest off.

A repeatable starting point for WordPress professionals.

If you build or maintain WordPress sites regularly, the same small requirements tend to appear again and again: email delivery, content duplication, code snippets, user testing, SVG support, login controls, exports and admin customisation.

Instead of finding and installing a different utility plugin every time one of those requirements appears, WP Extended gives you a familiar collection of tools you can configure around each project.

That makes WP Extended particularly useful for:

  • Freelancers building and maintaining client sites
  • Agencies managing multiple WordPress websites
  • Developers who want practical workflow and troubleshooting tools close at hand
  • Site owners who want additional WordPress functionality without accumulating unnecessary standalone plugins

Start free. Add more when your workflow needs it.

WP Extended Free is designed to be useful on its own. Many modules are available directly through the WordPress.org plugin, while some modules include additional Pro functionality or are available with WP Extended Pro.

You do not need to upgrade simply to understand how WP Extended works. Start with the tools your site needs today, and add more when your workflow requires them.

Compare WP Extended Free and Pro

What WP Extended is — and what it isn’t.

WP Extended focuses on the small but important WordPress jobs that often end up spread across numerous utility plugins. It is not intended to replace every specialist WordPress product.

For example, WP Extended is not positioned as a replacement for a complete:

  • Security platform
  • SEO platform
  • Ecommerce system
  • Backup service
  • Page builder
  • Performance or caching platform

Those products solve larger specialist problems. WP Extended gives the everyday WordPress jobs a more consistent home.

Why WP Extended?

  • Modular by design – Enable the individual capabilities your site needs instead of activating an entire feature set.
  • One familiar interface – Keep everyday WordPress tools together instead of remembering which standalone plugin controls which task.
  • Less plugin sprawl – Reduce reliance on multiple small utility plugins that each solve one narrow requirement.
  • Useful across multiple sites – Use the same familiar toolkit across different WordPress projects while configuring the modules differently for each one.
  • Built for everyday WordPress work – WP Extended focuses on practical tasks that site owners, developers, freelancers and agencies repeatedly encounter.

Extend WordPress. Not your plugin list.

Every small WordPress requirement should not automatically mean installing another plugin. Install WP Extended and enable the modules your site actually needs.

sections.installation:
Minimum Requirements

  • WordPress 5.6 or greater
  • PHP version 8.1 or greater
  • MySQL version 5.0 or greater

Installation

  1. Install using the WordPress built-in Plugin installer, or Extract the zip file and drop the contents in the wp-content/plugins/ directory of your WordPress installation.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Menu > WP Extended
  4. Enable plugin featured free modules

For documentation and tutorials visit our Knowledge Base.
sections.faq:
What is WP Extended?

WP Extended is a modular WordPress toolkit that brings a collection of practical admin, content, media, email, login, workflow and developer tools into one plugin. Instead of installing a separate plugin for every small requirement, you can enable the individual WP Extended modules your site needs.

Do I need to enable every module?

No. WP Extended is deliberately modular. Enable the modules that make sense for your site and leave everything else disabled. Different WordPress sites can use completely different combinations of WP Extended modules.

What makes WP Extended different from installing separate plugins?

Many everyday WordPress requirements are relatively small but still result in another standalone plugin being installed. WP Extended brings many of those utilities into one toolkit with a consistent interface and modular controls. This can reduce plugin sprawl and make common functionality easier to manage across your sites.

Which kinds of tools are included?

WP Extended includes tools for common WordPress workflows such as:

  • Duplicate posts and pages
  • SMTP email
  • Code snippets
  • SVG uploads
  • User switching
  • Content ordering
  • Exports
  • Maintenance mode
  • Custom login URLs
  • WordPress admin controls
  • Login protection
  • Media and workflow utilities

Module availability and functionality can vary between Free and Pro. See the full module list.

Is WP Extended a replacement for a full security plugin?

No. WP Extended includes practical login, privacy and WordPress-hardening tools, but it is not intended to replace a specialist security platform that provides features such as malware scanning, a firewall or advanced security monitoring.

Is WP Extended suitable for freelancers, agencies and developers?

Yes. WP Extended is particularly useful when the same small WordPress requirements keep appearing across different projects. You can use the same familiar toolkit across multiple sites while enabling a different set of modules according to each project’s needs.

Is WP Extended Free useful without Pro?

Yes. WP Extended Free includes a substantial collection of useful WordPress modules and is designed to stand on its own. Pro expands the toolkit with additional modules and advanced functionality where required. See what each version includes.

Will every module run on my site automatically?

No. Modules are individually enabled. If you do not need a particular capability, leave that module disabled.

How do I get support?

Contact the WP Extended team for support and general enquiries.

Where can I find documentation?

Documentation for WP Extended and individual modules is available on the WP Extended website.

Where can I see recent product changes?

The WP Extended changelog lists recent releases, fixes, new modules and product improvements.

  • Improved: Rollback Manager: The plugin and theme lists load faster: answers from WordPress.org are kept for 12 hours.
  • Fixed: Media Trash and Debug Mode: When wp-config.php cannot be written, the error now gives the exact line to add by hand, and stays on screen so it can be copied [Pro].

3.4.1 – 4 November 2026

Google Analytics loads with Consent Mode v2 set to denied, and the Facebook and Pinterest pixels wait until the visitor accepts cookies in Complianz, CookieYes or Cookie Notice. It is on by default for new installs; existing sites need to turn it on.

short_description: Replace your stack of WordPress plugins with one: SMTP, duplicate post, code snippets, custom login URL, maintenance mode, SVG upload and more.
description:
Stop installing another plugin for every small WordPress job.

WP Extended is a modular WordPress toolkit for the everyday jobs that usually send you searching for another plugin.

  • Need to duplicate a page?
  • Configure SMTP email?
  • Upload SVG files?
  • Manage code snippets?
  • Switch between users?
  • Change your WordPress login URL?
  • Reorder content?
  • Put a site into maintenance mode?

WP Extended brings these tools — and many more — into one consistent plugin. Enable what your site needs. Leave the rest off.

One toolkit. Individual modules.

WP Extended is not designed around activating everything. Each capability is managed as its own module, so you choose the tools that fit your site.

Enable a handful of modules on one WordPress site. Use a completely different combination on another. The same familiar toolkit sits underneath both.

With WP Extended you can:

  • Reduce reliance on small, single-purpose plugins
  • Enable only the modules your site actually needs
  • Manage everyday WordPress tools from one consistent interface
  • Keep familiar workflows across the sites you build and maintain
  • Start with useful functionality in the free plugin
  • Add Pro functionality later where your workflow requires it

Everyday WordPress jobs. One familiar toolkit.

  • Duplicate Posts & Pages – Duplicate existing posts and pages without rebuilding the content or layout from scratch. Useful for landing pages, service pages, repeatable content structures and editorial workflows.
  • SMTP Email – Configure WordPress email delivery through SMTP instead of adding another dedicated email plugin. Useful for site notifications, contact form delivery and transactional WordPress email.
  • Code Snippets – Manage PHP, HTML, CSS and JavaScript snippets without editing your theme files. Keep small site customisations easier to find and maintain.
  • SVG File Upload – Add SVG support to the WordPress media workflow for trusted logos, icons and scalable assets.
  • User Switching – Switch between WordPress user accounts more quickly when testing permissions, troubleshooting issues or supporting users.
  • Post Type Order – Reorder posts, pages and supported post types without writing custom code.
  • Export Posts & Export Users – Export WordPress content and user data for reporting, migrations, audits and other workflows.
  • Custom Login URL – Change the standard WordPress login path from the default URL.
  • Limit Login Attempts – Restrict repeated login attempts and reduce common brute-force login activity.
  • Maintenance Mode – Show visitors an appropriate maintenance page while work is taking place behind the scenes.
  • Menu Editor – Rename, reorder or hide WordPress admin menu items to create a cleaner admin experience.
  • Rollback Manager – Roll WordPress.org plugins or themes back to an earlier version when an update causes a problem.

Browse every WP Extended module

Built around the way you actually use WordPress.

A large toolkit does not mean every feature should be active. That is why WP Extended is modular.

Turn on SMTP on one site. Use Code Snippets and SVG uploads on another. Add content, admin or login tools where they make sense. Leave everything else disabled.

Turn on what you need. Leave the rest off.

A repeatable starting point for WordPress professionals.

If you build or maintain WordPress sites regularly, the same small requirements tend to appear again and again: email delivery, content duplication, code snippets, user testing, SVG support, login controls, exports and admin customisation.

Instead of finding and installing a different utility plugin every time one of those requirements appears, WP Extended gives you a familiar collection of tools you can configure around each project.

That makes WP Extended particularly useful for:

  • Freelancers building and maintaining client sites
  • Agencies managing multiple WordPress websites
  • Developers who want practical workflow and troubleshooting tools close at hand
  • Site owners who want additional WordPress functionality without accumulating unnecessary standalone plugins

Start free. Add more when your workflow needs it.

WP Extended Free is designed to be useful on its own. Many modules are available directly through the WordPress.org plugin, while some modules include additional Pro functionality or are available with WP Extended Pro.

You do not need to upgrade simply to understand how WP Extended works. Start with the tools your site needs today, and add more when your workflow requires them.

Compare WP Extended Free and Pro

What WP Extended is — and what it isn’t.

WP Extended focuses on the small but important WordPress jobs that often end up spread across numerous utility plugins. It is not intended to replace every specialist WordPress product.

For example, WP Extended is not positioned as a replacement for a complete:

  • Security platform
  • SEO platform
  • Ecommerce system
  • Backup service
  • Page builder
  • Performance or caching platform

Those products solve larger specialist problems. WP Extended gives the everyday WordPress jobs a more consistent home.

Why WP Extended?

  • Modular by design – Enable the individual capabilities your site needs instead of activating an entire feature set.
  • One familiar interface – Keep everyday WordPress tools together instead of remembering which standalone plugin controls which task.
  • Less plugin sprawl – Reduce reliance on multiple small utility plugins that each solve one narrow requirement.
  • Useful across multiple sites – Use the same familiar toolkit across different WordPress projects while configuring the modules differently for each one.
  • Built for everyday WordPress work – WP Extended focuses on practical tasks that site owners, developers, freelancers and agencies repeatedly encounter.

Extend WordPress. Not your plugin list.

Every small WordPress requirement should not automatically mean installing another plugin. Install WP Extended and enable the modules your site actually needs.

  • All modules
  • Documentation
  • Free vs Pro
  • Changelog
  • Support & contact

If you installed translation files by hand, rename them from wp-extended-{locale} to wpextended-{locale} — the text domain is now wpextended.
